newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel backs Warner-Lambert diabetes drug. [CORRECTED 22:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FDA panel backs Warner-Lambert diabetes drug. [CORRECTED 22:47 GMT]

text.p: A federal panel recommended Wednesday that the Food and Drug Administration approve the Warner-Lambert Co drug Rezulin (Corrects from "Ruzulin")
to treat the widespread Type II version of diabetes.
The FDA is not bound by the recommendations of its advisory committees but usually accepts their views.
Rezulin, given unanimous support by the FDA's Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee, is designed to treat a type of diabetes that cannot be adequately controlled with insulin.
The drug, discovered by the Japanese firm Sankyo Co Ltd, is made by Warner-Lambert's Parke Davis Pharmaceutical Research division. A similar drug has already been approved for marketing in Japan.
Warner-Lambert said it intended to ask the FDA early next year to approve Rezulin to treat other types of diabetes as well.

Company officials said Rezulin, taken as a tablet once a day, is able to increase the body's use of insulin, a hormone that is needed to convert sugar, starches and other foods into energy required for daily life.

Medical experts say Type II diabetes -- Type I is an autoimmune disease usually found in children -- is nearing epidemic proportions due to the rising number of older Americans and greater prevalence of obesity and sedentary lifestyles.
